newsitem.title: USA: Countdown starts for Sunday shuttle launch.
newsitem.headline: Countdown starts for Sunday shuttle launch.

text.p: The countdown began on Thursday for the launch of the space shuttle Atlantis on its fifth mission to Russia's Mir space station, NASA officials said.
The countdown clocks at the Kennedy Space Centre were set in motion at 7 a.m. EST (1200 GMT) for the planned 4:27 a.m. EST (0927 GMT) blastoff on Sunday.
NASA officials reported no technical problems with the $2 billion spaceship, although technicians had earlier replaced two faulty electronics boxes.
"The vehicle looks very, very good," said NASA test director John Guidi. "We are looking forward to continuing the countdown."
Forecasters said on Thursday they were expecting cold but favourable weather for the shuttle's departure. Conditions were expected to deteriorate on Monday and Tuesday, however.
If the shuttle is not off the ground by Tuesday it will have to wait for the launch of an unmanned Delta rocket.

A crew of six astronauts, led by three-time shuttle flier Mike Baker, arrived at the Kennedy Space Centre on Wednesday to begin final preparations. Joining Baker aboard Atlantis will be co-pilot Brent Jett, Jeff Wisoff, John Grunsfeld, Marsha Ivins and Jerry Linenger.
Linenger, a 42-year-old Navy captain and medical doctor, will take the place of U.S. astronaut John Blaha, who has been working aboard Russia's Mir since September.
During his four-month mission, Linenger will become the first American to take a spacewalk from Mir.
"Should be a great mission," he said after arriving at the launch site. "I'm really, really excited to go up there."
Linenger is hoping to end his mission on time in May so he can be present for the birth of his second child, due in late June.
